questions.extra_complexity: The two-layer design is necessary: GDScript owns semantic replay/biology and the POSIX store owns only opaque durable bytes. Repair R1 adds one explicit external acknowledgement floor rather than reconstructing authority from orphan files.
questions.duplicate_truth: No new ecology, field, Matter, Region or network authority truth was introduced. A7/A6/A4 remain the semantic writers; canonical handoff ticket/state machine are consumed unchanged. Store hashes are integrity/cursor evidence, not biological truth.
questions.implicit_owner: A8 explicitly separates logical A4 field owner/genesis from partition executor owner. Executor transitions are journaled and epoch-fenced. The external durable anchor is caller-owned and explicitly outside store trust; it is not silently inferred from CURRENT.
questions.coupling: A8 depends on the smallest existing surfaces required for scope: A7 save/load for the full coupled cut and canonical handoff contracts for transition legality. It does not depend on WorldEntityAggregate or production region internals.
questions.sibling_surface: Accepted A0-A7 runtime/tests, network handoff, registry/scheduler/control and project.godot are source-byte fenced against base main. A6/A7 restart, A5 repair oracles and mandatory A7 graphics remain in full exact verification.
questions.removable_code: No redundant alternate persistence/handoff implementation remains. Immutable orphan objects are intentionally tolerated before pointer publication; treating them as authority would reintroduce the reviewed P1.
questions.design_regression: Repair R1 strengthens the original crash model without changing biological or network semantics. It preserves both pre-pointer crash recovery and post-pointer ambiguous acknowledgement through equal/descendant external-anchor validation.
questions.redesign_if_larger_scope: For production A10, replace the local caller-owned anchor assumption with canonical production journal/consensus/region-authority contracts rather than promoting SnapshotStore as a distributed authority. Windows/power-loss qualification also requires a separate platform-specific durability contract.

remaining_bounded_risks: External durable anchor integrity/anti-rollback is an explicit caller/platform trust boundary; A8 proves separation from mutable store CURRENT, not adversarial rollback of every storage device.
POSIX file-lock/fsync/rename evidence qualifies the declared Linux local-store scope only.
A8 transfers the complete coupled research partition; production terrain/Matter/network binding remains A10 and is not inferred from this checkpoint.
Automatic multi-generation ecology is still outside the A7/A8 accepted claim boundary.
